class Tab:
    """One browser tab on one website, driven by one agent."""

    def __init__(self, page, site: dict):
        self.page = page
        self.site_id = site.get("siteId", "")
        self.base_url = site["url"].rstrip("/")
        self.credentials = site.get("credentials") or {}
        self.frames: list[tuple[int, int, object]] = []  # id range -> frame
        self.document = ""  # what `keep` files: the page as last read, a collected listing or a fetched file
        self.document_source = ""
        self.events: list[str] = []
        self.bad_status = 0
        self.loading: set = set()  # page, frame and data requests that have not come back yet
        self._watch(page)

    def _watch(self, page) -> None:
        page.on("dialog", lambda dialog: asyncio.ensure_future(self._on_dialog(dialog)))
        page.on("response", self._on_response)
        page.on("request", lambda request: self.loading.add(request) if request.resource_type in ("document", "xhr", "fetch") else None)
        page.on("requestfinished", lambda request: self.loading.discard(request))
        page.on("requestfailed", lambda request: self.loading.discard(request))

    async def renew(self) -> str:
        """Swap a broken tab for a fresh one in the same browser: same session and cookies, a clean page. A tab can get
        stuck ("frame was detached", loads that never finish) while the website itself is fine: in sandbox runs the
        investigators' tab kept timing out for minutes while a fresh tab on the same site loaded at once."""
        old = self.page
        page = await old.context.new_page()
        self.page, self.frames, self.loading, self.bad_status = page, [], set(), 0
        self._watch(page)
        try:
            await old.close()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass
        return await self.goto(self.base_url + "/")

    async def _on_dialog(self, dialog):
        self.events.append(f'the browser asked "{dialog.message}" ({dialog.type}); it was accepted')
        try:
            await dialog.accept()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass

    def _on_response(self, response):
        try:
            if response.request.is_navigation_request() and response.frame == self.page.main_frame:
                self.bad_status = response.status if response.status >= 500 else 0
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            pass

    async def settle(self):
        """Wait until the page, its frames and the data they fetch have arrived and nothing more is on its way."""
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        end, quiet = loop.time() + 12, None
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # let a click start its request
        while loop.time() < end:
            if self.loading:
                quiet = None
            elif quiet is None:
                quiet = loop.time()
            elif loop.time() - quiet >= 0.2:
                break
            await asyncio.sleep(0.04)
        else:
            self.loading.clear()  # a request that never ends must not hold up every later step
        for frame in list(self.page.frames):
            try:
                await frame.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=8000 if frame == self.page.main_frame else 3000)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                pass
        for _ in range(3):  # a server error page: retry the same address, as a person would press reload
            if not self.bad_status:
                break
            self.events.append(f"the server answered HTTP {self.bad_status}; reloaded")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.4)
            try:
                await self.page.reload(wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                break

    async def _frame_text(self, frame, start: int, depth: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
        try:
            prepared = await frame.evaluate(PREPARE_JS)
            if prepared["opened"]:
                await self.settle()  # lazy content of the sections just opened
            for name in prepared["closed"]:
                self.events.append(f'closed the popup "{name}"')
            shot = await frame.evaluate(SNAPSHOT_JS, start)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"{UNREADABLE}: {str(error)[:120]})", start
        self.frames.append((start, shot["next"], frame))
        text, following = shot["text"], shot["next"]
        for marker in re.findall(r"⟦FRAME:(\d+)⟧", text):
            inner = "(embedded document not loaded)"
            if depth < 4:
                try:
                    handle = await frame.query_selector(f'[data-aid="{marker}"]')
                    child = await handle.content_frame() if handle else None
                    if child:
                        try:
                            await child.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", timeout=4000)
                        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                            pass
                        inner, following = await self._frame_text(child, following, depth + 1)
                except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                    inner = f"(embedded document could not be read: {str(error)[:120]})"
            block = "┌── embedded document: " if inner.strip() else "┌── embedded document (empty): "
            text = text.replace(f"⟦FRAME:{marker}⟧", block, 1).replace(
                block, block, 1)
            # the marker line carries the frame's title; append the frame's content under it
            lines = text.split("\n")
            for index, line in enumerate(lines):
                if line.startswith(block) and not line.endswith("⁣"):
                    lines[index] = line + "⁣"
                    lines.insert(index + 1, "\n".join("│ " + row for row in inner.split("\n")) + "\n└── end of embedded document")
                    break
            text = "\n".join(lines)
        return text.replace("⁣", ""), following

    async def read(self) -> str:
        """The current page as text, with fresh element ids."""
        for _ in range(4):  # a page that navigates while it is read is read again
            await self.settle()
            self.frames = []
            text, _ = await self._frame_text(self.page.main_frame, 1, 0)
            if not text.startswith(UNREADABLE):
                break
        try:
            title = await self.page.title()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            title = ""
        self.document = f"url: {self.page.url}\ntitle: {clean_text(title)}\n{clean_text(text)}"
        self.document_source = self.page.url
        return self.document

    async def observe(self) -> str:
        text = await self.read()
        if len(text) > MAX_OBSERVATION:
            text = text[:MAX_OBSERVATION] + f"\n… (page text cut here; {len(text) - MAX_OBSERVATION} more characters. `keep` files the whole page.)"
        return text

    def take_events(self) -> list[str]:
        events, self.events = self.events, []
        return events

    async def _modal_is_open(self) -> bool:
        """Whether a page-level dialog now prevents ordinary controls from being used."""
        script = """() => {
          const visible = el => { const s = getComputedStyle(el); return !el.hidden && el.getAttribute('aria-hidden') !== 'true' && s.display !== 'none' && s.visibility !== 'hidden'; };
          return [...document.querySelectorAll('dialog[open],[aria-modal="true"]')]
            .some(el => visible(el) && (el.tagName !== 'DIALOG' || el.matches(':modal')));
        }"""
        for frame in self.page.frames:
            try:
                if await frame.evaluate(script):
                    return True
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                continue
        return False

    def _locator(self, aid):
        try:
            number = int(aid)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return None
        for start, end, frame in self.frames:
            if start <= number < end:
                return frame.locator(f'[data-aid="{number}"]')
        return None

    async def _describe(self, locator) -> dict:
        info = await self._describe_raw(locator)
        info["name"] = clean_text(info["name"])[:80]  # without the invisible characters pages hide in names
        return info

    async def _describe_raw(self, locator) -> dict:
        return await locator.evaluate(
            """el => ({tag: el.tagName, type: (el.getAttribute('type') || '').toLowerCase(), href: el.href || '',
                      disabled: el.disabled === true || !!el.closest('fieldset[disabled],[inert]'),
                      name: (el.innerText || el.value || el.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, 400)})""")

    async def click(self, aid) -> str:
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more; read the current page"
        info = await self._describe(locator)
        if info["disabled"]:
            return f"[{aid}] is disabled (inside a locked or inert area?); nothing happened"
        before = self.page.url
        try:
            await locator.click(timeout=2500)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  hidden in a collapsed menu, or covered: activate it directly
            try:
                await locator.evaluate("el => el.click()")
            except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                return f"could not click [{aid}]: {str(error)[:150]}"
        await self.settle()
        if await self._modal_is_open():
            return "the page now has a modal dialog; read it before acting behind it"
        moved = self.page.url != before
        return f'clicked [{aid}] "{info["name"]}"' + (f"; now at {self.page.url}" if moved else "")

    async def fill(self, aid, text: str, enter: bool = False) -> str:
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        try:
            await locator.fill(str(text), timeout=2500)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"could not fill [{aid}]: {str(error)[:150]}"
        if enter:
            await locator.press("Enter")
            await self.settle()
        if await self._modal_is_open():
            return "the page now has a modal dialog; read it before acting behind it"
        return f"filled [{aid}]" + (" and pressed Enter" if enter else "")

    async def select(self, aid, value: str) -> str:
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        wanted = str(value)
        for attempt in ({"value": wanted}, {"label": wanted}):
            try:
                await locator.select_option(timeout=2000, **attempt)
                await self.settle()
                if await self._modal_is_open():
                    return "the page now has a modal dialog; read it before acting behind it"
                return f'selected "{wanted}" in [{aid}]'
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                continue
        options = await locator.evaluate("el => [...(el.options || [])].map(o => o.value + '=' + o.textContent.trim())")
        loose = [o.split("=", 1)[0] for o in options if wanted.lower() in o.lower()]
        if len(loose) == 1:
            await locator.select_option(value=loose[0])
            await self.settle()
            return f'selected "{loose[0]}" in [{aid}]'
        return f'[{aid}] has no option "{wanted}"; options: {"; ".join(options)[:600]}'

    async def set(self, aid, value) -> str:
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        info = await self._describe(locator)
        if info["disabled"]:
            return f"[{aid}] is disabled; nothing happened"
        try:
            if info["type"] in ("checkbox", "radio"):
                wanted = bool(value)
                try:
                    await locator.set_checked(wanted, timeout=1500)
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  covered or restyled: toggle it as its label would
                    if await locator.is_checked() != wanted:
                        await locator.evaluate("el => el.click()")
                if await locator.is_checked() != wanted:
                    return f"[{aid}] did not change; it is still {'unchecked' if wanted else 'checked'}"
            else:  # a slider or another input whose value is set in one go
                await locator.evaluate(
                    """(el, v) => { const proto = Object.getPrototypeOf(el); const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(proto, 'value');
                                   d && d.set ? d.set.call(el, String(v)) : el.value = String(v);
                                   el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); el.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); }""",
                    value)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"could not set [{aid}]: {str(error)[:150]}"
        await self.settle()
        if await self._modal_is_open():
            return "the page now has a modal dialog; read it before acting behind it"
        return f"set [{aid}] to {value}"

    def _on_site(self, url: str) -> bool:
        return urlparse(url).netloc == urlparse(self.base_url).netloc

    async def goto(self, url: str) -> str:
        target = urljoin(self.page.url if self._on_site(self.page.url) else self.base_url + "/", str(url).strip())
        if not self._on_site(target):
            return f"{target} is not on this website; you only work on {self.base_url}"
        try:
            await self.page.goto(target, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=20000)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"could not open {target}: {str(error)[:150]}"
        await self.settle()
        return f"opened {self.page.url}"

    async def back(self) -> str:
        try:
            await self.page.go_back(wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"could not go back: {str(error)[:120]}"
        await self.settle()
        return f"went back to {self.page.url}"

    async def reload(self) -> str:
        try:
            await self.page.reload(wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=15000)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"could not reload: {str(error)[:120]}"
        await self.settle()
        return "reloaded the page"

    async def login(self) -> str:
        if not self.credentials.get("password"):
            return "there are no credentials for this website"
        outcome = "no password field on this page"
        for frame in self.page.frames:
            try:
                outcome = await frame.evaluate(LOGIN_JS, [self.credentials.get("username", ""), self.credentials["password"]])
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                continue
            if outcome == "ok":
                await frame.locator("[data-login-password]").first.press("Enter")
                await self.settle()
                return f"entered the credentials and submitted the login form; now at {self.page.url}"
        return outcome

    async def collect(self, aid, max_pages: int = 10) -> str:
        """Follow the paging control the model chose until it is gone, and return every page as one document."""
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        info = await self._describe(locator)
        if not info["name"]:
            return f"[{aid}] has no label to follow from page to page"
        first = self.document
        pages, seen = [first], {first}
        for _ in range(max(1, min(int(max_pages or 10), 30)) - 1):
            control = None
            for _, _, frame in self.frames:
                candidates = frame.locator("a[href], button, [role=button], [role=link]")
                for index in range(min(await candidates.count(), 200)):
                    candidate = candidates.nth(index)
                    try:
                        label = clean_text(await candidate.evaluate("el => el.innerText || el.value || el.getAttribute('aria-label') || ''"))[:80]
                        if label == info["name"] and (await candidate.evaluate("el => el.tagName")) == info["tag"] \
                                and not await candidate.evaluate("el => el.disabled === true"):
                            control = candidate
                            break
                    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                        continue
                if control:
                    break
            if control is None:
                break
            try:
                await control.click(timeout=2500)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                try:
                    await control.evaluate("el => el.click()")
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                    break
            await self.read()
            if self.document in seen:
                break
            seen.add(self.document)
            pages.append(self.document)
        if len(pages) == 1:
            return f'"{info["name"]}" led to no further page; the list is the page you see'
        # A button may append rows in place rather than lead to a new page. Compare page bodies without generated
        # element ids or the changing paging control: both change between reads even when every earlier row remains.
        def body(page: str) -> str:
            return "\n".join(line for line in without_ids(page).splitlines()
                             if not re.match(r'(?:button|link) "', line.strip()))

        bodies = [body(page) for page in pages]
        grows = (len(pages) > 1 and info["tag"].upper() != "A"
                 and all(later.startswith(earlier) and len(later) >= len(earlier)
                         for earlier, later in zip(bodies, bodies[1:])))
        if grows:  # a "load more" control: the last page holds every row
            self.document = pages[-1]
            return f'followed "{info["name"]}" {len(pages) - 1} time(s); the list is now complete on the page'
        self.document = "\n".join(f"{PAGE_BREAK} {number} =====\n{page}" for number, page in enumerate(pages, 1))
        return (f'followed "{info["name"]}" through {len(pages)} page(s); you are on the last one. COLLECTED DOCUMENT '
                f"(file it with keep if it is relevant):\n{without_ids(self.document)[:MAX_OBSERVATION * 2]}")

    async def fetch(self, aid) -> str:
        """Download what the chosen link points to and read it as a document."""
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        target = await locator.evaluate("el => el.href || el.src || el.getAttribute('data-url') || el.getAttribute('formaction') || ''")
        if not target:
            return f"[{aid}] has no address to download"
        target = urljoin(self.page.url, target)
        if not self._on_site(target):
            return f"{target} is not on this website"
        try:
            response = await self.page.context.request.get(target, timeout=20000)
            data = await response.body()
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"could not download {target}: {str(error)[:150]}"
        name = urlparse(target).path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] or "download"
        disposition = response.headers.get("content-disposition", "")
        named = re.search(r'filename\*?=(?:UTF-8\'\')?"?([^";]+)', disposition)
        if named:
            name = named.group(1)
        self.document = document_text(data, response.headers.get("content-type", ""), name)
        self.document_source = target
        return (f"downloaded {name} (HTTP {response.status}, {len(data)} bytes). DOCUMENT (file it with keep if it is "
                f"relevant):\n{self.document[:MAX_OBSERVATION * 2]}")

"""The generic action verifier must expose silent portal failures to the model."""
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import llm  # noqa: E402
from worker import Agent, state_fingerprint  # noqa: E402


class FakeTab:
    def __init__(self, change_on_fill: bool):
        self.base_url = "http://portal.test"
        self.page = SimpleNamespace(url=self.base_url, main_frame=SimpleNamespace(evaluate=self._alive))
        self.document, self.document_source = "", ""
        self.change_on_fill = change_on_fill
        self.view = 'url: http://portal.test\ntitle: Form\n[1] input "Name" value=""'

    async def _alive(self, script):
        return True

    async def observe(self):
        return self.view

    def take_events(self):
        return []

    async def fill(self, aid, text, enter=False):
        if self.change_on_fill:
            self.view = f'url: http://portal.test\ntitle: Form\n[1] input "Name" value="{text}"'
        return f"filled [{aid}]"


class ActionVerification(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_agent(self, change_on_fill: bool):
        replies = [
            {"thought": "", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "Ada"}]},
            {"thought": "", "actions": [{"do": "done", "summary": "checked"}]},
        ]
        asked = []

        async def model(messages, **kwargs):
            asked.append(messages[-1]["content"])
            return replies.pop(0)

        with patch.object(llm, "chat_json", model):
            outcome = await Agent("test", FakeTab(change_on_fill), "system", lambda: "job", max_steps=4).run()
        return outcome, asked

    async def test_changed_form_state_is_reported(self):
        outcome, asked = await self.run_agent(True)
        self.assertTrue(outcome["done"])
        self.assertIn("verification: fill visibly changed the page state", asked[1])

    async def test_silent_noop_is_reported_with_a_recovery_hint(self):
        outcome, asked = await self.run_agent(False)
        self.assertTrue(outcome["done"])
        self.assertIn("verification: fill caused no visible page change", asked[1])
        self.assertIn("instead of repeating it blindly", asked[1])

    def test_generated_action_ids_do_not_count_as_a_state_change(self):
        first = 'url: http://portal.test\n[1] button "Continue"'
        reread = 'url: http://portal.test\n[48] button "Continue"'
        self.assertEqual(state_fingerprint(first), state_fingerprint(reread))


class LoopDetectionAndChaining(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    """Tests for repeated-action loop warnings, stale-ID chaining protection, and stuck-tab renewal."""

    async def test_repeating_same_action_on_unchanged_page_injects_loop_warning_on_third_repeat(self):
        tab = FakeTab(change_on_fill=False)
        replies = [
            {"thought": "try 1", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "Same"}]},
            {"thought": "try 2", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "Same"}]},
            {"thought": "try 3", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "Same"}]},
            {"thought": "stop", "actions": [{"do": "done", "summary": "stopped"}]},
        ]

"""Synthetic review-page variations for the last, non-submitting portal check."""
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from calculator import Bid, Line
from preflight import check


def bid() -> Bid:
    line = Line("1", "M-1", 40, unit_price=Decimal("12.50"), lead_time_weeks=3)
    return Bid("T-0001", "bid", Decimal("2.5"), [line], Decimal("500.00"))


class ReviewPages(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_renamed_and_reordered_review_fields_still_pass(self):
        page = "Bestellübersicht\nEUR 500,00\nArtikel 1 / M-1\nVorgang T-0001\n[8] button \"Endgültig bestätigen\""
        report = check(page, bid(), "T-0001")
        self.assertTrue(report.ready, report.text())

"""The generic action verifier must expose silent portal failures to the model."""
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import llm  # noqa: E402
from worker import Agent, state_fingerprint  # noqa: E402


class FakeTab:
    def __init__(self, change_on_fill: bool):
        self.base_url = "http://portal.test"
        self.page = SimpleNamespace(url=self.base_url, main_frame=SimpleNamespace(evaluate=self._alive))
        self.document, self.document_source = "", ""
        self.change_on_fill = change_on_fill
        self.view = 'url: http://portal.test\ntitle: Form\n[1] input "Name" value=""'

    async def _alive(self, script):
        return True

    async def observe(self):
        return self.view

    def take_events(self):
        return []

    async def fill(self, aid, text, enter=False):
        if self.change_on_fill:
            self.view = f'url: http://portal.test\ntitle: Form\n[1] input "Name" value="{text}"'
        return f"filled [{aid}]"


class ActionVerification(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_agent(self, change_on_fill: bool):
        replies = [
            {"thought": "", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "Ada"}]},
            {"thought": "", "actions": [{"do": "done", "summary": "checked"}]},
        ]
        asked = []

        async def model(messages, **kwargs):
            asked.append(messages[-1]["content"])
            return replies.pop(0)

        with patch.object(llm, "chat_json", model):
            outcome = await Agent("test", FakeTab(change_on_fill), "system", lambda: "job", max_steps=4).run()
        return outcome, asked

    async def test_changed_form_state_is_reported(self):
        outcome, asked = await self.run_agent(True)
        self.assertTrue(outcome["done"])
        self.assertIn("verification: fill visibly changed the page state", asked[1])

    async def test_silent_noop_is_reported_with_a_recovery_hint(self):
        outcome, asked = await self.run_agent(False)
        self.assertTrue(outcome["done"])
        self.assertIn("verification: fill caused no visible page change", asked[1])
        self.assertIn("instead of repeating it blindly", asked[1])

    def test_generated_action_ids_do_not_count_as_a_state_change(self):
        first = 'url: http://portal.test\n[1] button "Continue"'
        reread = 'url: http://portal.test\n[48] button "Continue"'
        self.assertEqual(state_fingerprint(first), state_fingerprint(reread))


class LoopDetectionAndChaining(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    """Tests for repeated-action loop warnings, stale-ID chaining protection, and stuck-tab renewal."""

    async def test_repeating_same_action_on_unchanged_page_injects_loop_warning_on_third_repeat(self):
        tab = FakeTab(change_on_fill=False)
        replies = [
            {"thought": "try 1", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "Same"}]},
            {"thought": "try 2", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "Same"}]},
            {"thought": "try 3", "actions": [{"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "Same"}]},
            {"thought": "stop", "actions": [{"do": "done", "summary": "stopped"}]},
        ]

entries.description: A run's log lines, in time order, each with its time on the run's clock and its stream. Streams: stdout and stderr (your agent system), setup (the platform: install, the free models' warm-up), input (what the browsers received; run_inputs reads them better, so they're left out unless you ask). Narrow with from/to (e.g. from 02:10 to 02:40), grep, browser; tail for the last lines; page with after. About 30 tokens a line.

from.description: The earliest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

to.description: The latest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

"""What an agent really did on its website, and the gate that reads it before a question is closed.

A model that says "I searched everywhere" proves nothing. The agent loop writes this record itself, from the actions
it carried out: the pages it opened, the text it typed into search and filter fields, the lists it followed and how
each of them ended. Closing a question is then checked against the record:

- a list that stopped at its page limit while its paging control was still there is incomplete, so no question is
  closed on this website until the rest is read;
- "absent" is the one claim the case file cannot check, so it is answered with the record first: a search without
  hits covers that search term in that place and nothing more.

Every refusal is bounded. After `LIMIT` of them a question closes anyway: the gate may cost an agent a few turns,
it must never keep a run from finishing. Nothing here knows a website; where to look next stays the model's call.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from urllib.parse import urlparse

LIMIT = 2  # refusals per question
SHOWN = 12  # entries of each kind in the record an agent is shown


@dataclass
class ListRun:
    where: str  # the address the list was followed from
    control: str  # the label of the paging control
    pages: int
    capped: bool  # it stopped at the page limit and the control was still there


def _short(address: str) -> str:
    """An address without its host: the agent works one website."""
    parts = urlparse(address)
    return (parts.path or "/") + (f"?{parts.query}" if parts.query else "") + (f"#{parts.fragment}" if parts.fragment else "")


class Ledger:
    def __init__(self):
        self.views: dict[str, str] = {}  # address -> title, in the order of the first visit
        self.queries: list[tuple[str, str]] = []  # (address, text typed), each once
        self.lists: list[ListRun] = []
        self.moves = 0  # browser actions that visibly changed the page
        self.refused: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}  # question -> (refusals so far, size of the record at the last)

    # ---- written by the agent loop ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def saw(self, page: str) -> None:
        """A page as the agent read it: its first lines carry the address and the title."""
        address = re.match(r"url: (\S+)", page or "")
        if address and address.group(1) not in self.views:
            title = re.search(r"^title: (.*)$", page, re.M)

async def collect(self, aid, max_pages: int = 10) -> str:
        """Follow the paging control the model chose until it is gone, and return every page as one document.
        `last_collect` records how it ended: a list that stopped at the page limit with its control still there is
        not complete, and the answer says so instead of passing for the whole list."""
        self.last_collect = None
        locator = self._locator(aid)
        if locator is None or await locator.count() == 0:
            return f"there is no element [{aid}] on the page any more"
        info = await self._describe(locator)
        if not info["name"]:
            return f"[{aid}] has no label to follow from page to page"
        first, start = self.document, self.page.url
        pages, seen = [first], {first}
        limit = max(1, min(int(max_pages or 10), 30))

        async def next_control():
            for _, _, frame in self.frames:
                candidates = frame.locator("a[href], button, [role=button], [role=link]")
                for index in range(min(await candidates.count(), 200)):
                    candidate = candidates.nth(index)
                    try:
                        label = clean_text(await candidate.evaluate("el => el.innerText || el.value || el.getAttribute('aria-label') || ''"))[:80]
                        if label == info["name"] and (await candidate.evaluate("el => el.tagName")) == info["tag"] \
                                and not await candidate.evaluate("el => el.disabled === true"):
                            return candidate
                    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                        continue
            return None

        capped = False
        for turn in range(limit):
            control = await next_control()
            if control is None:
                break
            if turn == limit - 1:  # the page limit ended this, not the list: the control is still there
                capped = True
                break
            try:
                await control.click(timeout=2500)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                try:
                    await control.evaluate("el => el.click()")
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                    break
            await self.read()
            if self.document in seen:
                break
            seen.add(self.document)
            pages.append(self.document)
        if len(pages) == 1:
            return f'"{info["name"]}" led to no further page; the list is the page you see'
        # A button may append rows in place rather than lead to a new page. Compare page bodies without generated
        # element ids or the changing paging control: both change between reads even when every earlier row remains.
        def body(page: str) -> str:
            return "\n".join(line for line in without_ids(page).splitlines()
                             if not re.match(r'(?:button|link) "', line.strip()))

        bodies = [body(page) for page in pages]
        grows = (len(pages) > 1 and info["tag"].upper() != "A"
                 and all(later.startswith(earlier) and len(later) >= len(earlier)
                         for earlier, later in zip(bodies, bodies[1:])))
        if grows:  # a "load more" control: the last page holds every row
            self.document = pages[-1]
            return f'followed "{info["name"]}" {len(pages) - 1} time(s); the list is now complete on the page'
        self.document = "\n".join(f"{PAGE_BREAK} {number} =====\n{page}" for number, page in enumerate(pages, 1))
        return (f'followed "{info["name"]}" through {len(pages)} page(s); you are on the last one. COLLECTED DOCUMENT '
                f"(file it with keep if it is relevant):\n{without_ids(self.document)[:MAX_OBSERVATION * 2]}")

    async def fetch(self, aid) -> str:
        """Download what the chosen link points to and read it as a document."""

"""The coverage record and the gate in front of closing a question, on invented pages (no scenario values)."""
import os
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import llm  # noqa: E402
from coverage import LIMIT, Ledger  # noqa: E402
from worker import Agent  # noqa: E402


def page(path: str, title: str = "List") -> str:
    return f'url: http://site.test{path}\ntitle: {title}\n[1] input "Search" value=""'


class Record(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_it_holds_each_page_and_each_typed_text_once(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        for text in (page("/inbox", "Inbox"), page("/inbox", "Inbox"), page("/archive", "Archive"), "(the page could not be read)"):
            ledger.saw(text)
        ledger.typed("http://site.test/inbox", "T-0001")
        ledger.typed("http://site.test/inbox", "t-0001 ")
        ledger.typed("http://site.test/archive", "T-0001")
        ledger.typed("http://site.test/archive", "")
        self.assertEqual(list(ledger.views.values()), ["Inbox", "Archive"])
        self.assertEqual(len(ledger.queries), 2)
        report = ledger.report()
        self.assertIn('"Archive" /archive', report)
        self.assertIn('"T-0001" at /inbox', report)
        self.assertIn("lists followed page by page (0): none", report)

    def test_a_list_cut_at_its_page_limit_stays_incomplete_until_the_same_control_reaches_the_end(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.followed({"where": "http://site.test/qa", "control": "Next", "pages": 3, "capped": True})
        self.assertEqual([run.control for run in ledger.incomplete()], ["Next"])
        ledger.followed({"where": "http://site.test/qa?page=3", "control": "Next", "pages": 2, "capped": False})
        self.assertEqual(ledger.incomplete(), [])
        ledger.followed(None)  # a collect that never started leaves no trace
        self.assertEqual(len(ledger.lists), 2)


class Gate(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_complete_passes_when_no_list_was_cut_short(self):
        self.assertIsNone(Ledger().gate("clarifications", "complete"))

    def test_nothing_is_closed_over_a_list_that_stopped_at_its_limit(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.followed({"where": "http://site.test/qa", "control": "Next", "pages": 5, "capped": True})
        for status in ("complete", "absent"):
            refusal = ledger.gate("q-" + status, status)
            self.assertIn("stopped at its limit of 5 page(s)", refusal)
            self.assertIn("higher max_pages", refusal)
        ledger.followed({"where": "http://site.test/qa?page=5", "control": "Next", "pages": 4, "capped": False})
        self.assertIsNone(ledger.gate("q-complete", "complete"))

    def test_absent_is_answered_with_the_record_first_and_accepted_after_a_further_search(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.saw(page("/inbox", "Inbox"))
        ledger.typed("http://site.test/inbox", "T-0001")
        refusal = ledger.gate("discount", "absent")
        self.assertIn("not closed yet", refusal)
        self.assertIn('"T-0001" at /inbox', refusal)  # the record is what the agent did, not what it says
        self.assertIn("covers only that search term in that place", refusal)
        again = ledger.gate("discount", "absent")
        self.assertIn("nothing new was searched since the last check", again)
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.gate("discount", "absent")
        ledger.saw(page("/archive", "Archive"))
        self.assertIsNone(ledger.gate("discount", "absent"))

    def test_every_question_is_challenged_on_its_own(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.gate("discount", "absent")
        ledger.moved()
        self.assertIsNone(ledger.gate("discount", "absent"))
        self.assertIsNotNone(ledger.gate("index:X-1", "absent"))

    def test_the_gate_is_bounded_so_it_can_never_hold_a_run(self):
        ledger = Ledger()
        ledger.followed({"where": "http://site.test/huge", "control": "Next", "pages": 30, "capped": True})
        refusals = [ledger.gate("discount", "absent") for _ in range(LIMIT + 2)]
        self.assertEqual([refusal is None for refusal in refusals], [False] * LIMIT + [True, True])


class FakeTab:
    """As much of a Tab as the agent loop touches: a mailbox with two folders, a search field and a paged list."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.base_url = "http://site.test"
        self.page = SimpleNamespace(url=self.base_url + "/inbox", main_frame=SimpleNamespace(evaluate=self._alive))
        self.document, self.document_source = "", ""
        self.last_collect = None
        self.query = ""

    async def _alive(self, script):
        return True

    async def observe(self):
        return f'url: {self.page.url}\ntitle: Mail\n[1] input "Search" value="{self.query}"\n[2] link "Archive"\n[3] link "Next"'

    def take_events(self):
        return []

    async def fill(self, aid, text, enter=False):
        self.query = text
        return f"filled [{aid}]"

    async def click(self, aid):
        self.page.url = self.base_url + "/archive"
        return f"clicked [{aid}]"

    async def collect(self, aid, max_pages=10):
        capped = int(max_pages) < 4
        self.last_collect = {"where": self.page.url, "control": "Next", "pages": min(int(max_pages), 4), "capped": capped}
        return "followed" + (" THE LIST IS NOT COMPLETE" if capped else "")


class InTheAgentLoop(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_agent(self, replies):
        asked, closed = [], []

        async def model(messages, **kwargs):
            asked.append(messages[-1]["content"])
            return replies.pop(0)

        async def answer(action):
            closed.append((action["question"], action["status"]))
            return f"question {action['question']} closed as {action['status']}"

        agent = Agent("mail", FakeTab(), "system", lambda: "job", extra={"answer": answer}, max_steps=len(replies) + 1)
        with patch.object(llm, "chat_json", model):
            await agent.run()
        return agent, asked, closed

    @staticmethod
    def turn(*actions):
        return {"thought": "", "actions": list(actions)}

    async def test_absent_after_one_search_is_held_back_until_the_agent_searched_further(self):
        absent = {"do": "answer", "question": "discount", "status": "absent", "note": "searched everywhere"}
        agent, asked, closed = await self.run_agent([
            self.turn({"do": "fill", "id": 1, "text": "T-0001", "enter": True}),
            self.turn(absent),

class Script:
    """Stands in for llm.chat_json: answers each agent, named by `label`, with its next scripted reply."""

    def __init__(self, **replies):
        self.replies, self.asked = replies, []

    async def __call__(self, messages, *, think=True, max_tokens=6000, label=""):
        self.asked.append({"label": label, "think": think, "system": messages[0]["content"],
                           "user": messages[-1]["content"]})
        return self.replies[label].pop(0) if self.replies.get(label) else {}

    def turns(self, label: str) -> list[dict]:
        return [call for call in self.asked if call["label"] == label]


def done(**fields) -> dict:
    return {"thought": "", "actions": [{"do": "done", **fields}]}

by value await tab.select(self.control(page, "select", "Unit").id, "Boxes") # by label await tab.set(self.control(page, "radio", "Express").id, True) await tab.set(self.control(page, "checkbox", "Gift wrap").id, True) await tab.set(self.control(page, "checkbox", "Send me updates").id, False) await tab.set(self.control(page, "slider", "Priority").id, 4) page = await tab.observe() # @@ -205,7 +206,17 @@ async def submit_bid(tender_tab: Tab, mail_tab: Tab | None, bid: Bid, context: d
         review = check_review(await tender_tab.observe(), bid, reference)
         if not review.ready:
             return review.text() + "\nFinal submission was not pressed."
-        return await tender_tab.click(action.get("id"))

+            final["page"] = ""
+        final["clicked"] = True
+        clerk.deadline = 0  # ends the agent loop before its next model call
+        return result
 
     def heading() -> str:
         left = int(deadline - time.time())
@@ -236,6 +247,9 @@ async def submit_bid(tender_tab: Tab, mail_tab: Tab | None, bid: Bid, context: d
     outcome = await clerk.run()
     receipt = str(outcome.get("answer") or "").strip()
     notes = str(outcome.get("summary") or "")
+    if final["clicked"]:  # submitted: the confirmation was read in code, no model turn after the click
+        receipt = receipt or final["page"][:1500]
+        return {"submitted": True, "receipt": receipt, "notes": notes or "submitted; confirmation read without the model"}
     if not outcome.get("done"):
         notes = (notes + " " if notes else "") + f"stopped after {outcome.get('steps', 0)} steps without a confirmation"
     return {"submitted": bool(outcome.get("done") and receipt), "receipt": receipt, "notes": notes}

feat(starter-kit): gate question closing on what the agent really searched

A model saying "I searched everywhere" is not proof. The agent loop now
keeps a coverage record from the actions it carried out (pages opened,
text typed, lists followed and how they ended) and checks it before a
question is closed:

- coverage.py: the record and the gate. "absent" is answered with the
  record first and accepted after a further search; nothing is closed
  over a list that stopped at its page limit. Every refusal is bounded
  (2 per question) so the gate can never hold a run.
- browser_env.Tab.collect: says when the page limit cut a list short
  while its paging control was still there (last_collect), instead of
  passing a partial list off as the whole one.
- browser_env.Tab.fill: reads the field back and reports when the form
  reformatted or refused the value.
- sanity.py: plugin "coverage_gate" (switch off with SANITY_CHECKS).

Not measured in the sandbox yet; unit and browser tests green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

feat(starter-kit): hold the final step until the review shows the bid

preflight.check now tells "the page shows something wrong" (blockers)
from "the page does not show what a review must show" (unproven: tender
reference, offered positions, calculated total). A final confirmation on
a page that does not show the bid confirms something nobody compared, so
finalize sends the clerk to a page that does.

That wait is bounded (UNPROVEN_REFUSALS = 2) and skipped when time is
short: a signed bid scores, an unsigned one does not. Explicit errors
and empty required controls still block without limit. A unit price the
review does not list only warns; a no_bid needs no total.

sanity plugin "summary_check" switches the new blocking off.

Not measured in the sandbox yet; unit tests green.

    async def finalize(action: dict) -> str:
        nonlocal review, held_back
        # Navigation, expiry and server validation can invalidate an earlier review, so inspect it again.
        review = await look()
        if review.blockers:
            return review.text() + "\nFinal submission was not pressed."
        if review.unproven:
            # The page does not show the bid, so pressing here would confirm something nobody compared. The clerk
            # is sent to a page that does show it, a bounded number of times and never when time is short.
            short = deadline - time.time() < WRAP_UP
            if held_back < UNPROVEN_REFUSALS and not short:
                held_back += 1
                return review.text() + "\nFinal submission was not pressed."
            print("[submit] final step pressed without full review evidence ("
                  + ("time is short" if short else f"held back {held_back} time(s)") + "): "
                  + " | ".join(review.unproven), flush=True)
        result = await tender_tab.click(action.get("id"))
        # Submitting ends the run and with it the run token: every later model call fails ("expired/unknown run
        # token" in sandbox runs 6da03229, 8184b178, 3c3568bb). So the confirmation is read here, in code, and the
        # clerk stops without another model turn.
        try:
            final["page"] = await asyncio.wait_for(tender_tab.observe(), 20)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            final["page"] = ""
        final["clicked"] = True
        clerk.deadline = 0  # ends the agent loop before its next model call
        return result

def _merge(store: dict, key, record: dict) -> list[tuple[str, object, object]]:
    """The value filed last is the one in use. Returns where it replaced a different one, as (field, earlier,
    later): two documents that disagree about the same record are a conflict to report, not to overwrite in
    silence (a draft, a superseded revision and a look-alike record all look like this)."""
    old = store.setdefault(key, {})
    replaced = []
    for name, value in record.items():

                    and str(earlier).strip().casefold() != str(value).strip().casefold():
                replaced.append((name, earlier, value))
            old[name] = value
    return replaced

"""Two filed documents that disagree about the same record are reported, on invented values (no scenario values)."""
import json
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import casefile  # noqa: E402


def case() -> casefile.CaseFile:
    return casefile.CaseFile("brief", {"tender_reference": "TEST-0001", "scenario_date": "2030-01-01"})


class Conflicts(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_later_document_that_adds_fields_or_repeats_values_is_no_conflict(self):
        facts = case()
        facts.merge("material", {"materials": [{"material_number": "M-1", "bore_mm": 50, "allocation_mass": "1,25"}]})
        account = facts.merge("material", {"materials": [{"material_number": "M-1", "bore_mm": "50", "stroke_mm": 200,
                                                         "allocation_mass": "1.25", "free_stock": None}]})
        self.assertNotIn("CONFLICT", account)  # the same number in another notation is the same value
        self.assertEqual(facts.conflicts, [])
        self.assertEqual(facts.materials["M-1"]["stroke_mm"], 200)

    def test_a_different_value_for_the_same_record_is_reported_and_kept_on_file(self):
        facts = case()
        facts.merge("material", {"materials": [{"material_number": "M-1", "free_stock": 120, "description": "Cylinder"}]})
        account = facts.merge("material", {"materials": [{"material_number": "M-1", "free_stock": 99,
                                                         "description": "Cylinder, double acting"}]})
        self.assertTrue(account.startswith("CONFLICT WITH AN EARLIER DOCUMENT"), account)
        self.assertIn("material M-1 free_stock: 120 on an earlier document, 99 on this one", account)
        self.assertIn("M-1: free_stock=99", account)  # the ordinary account still follows
        self.assertNotIn("description", " ".join(facts.conflicts))  # wording is not a fact
        self.assertEqual(facts.materials["M-1"]["free_stock"], 99)  # the value filed last is in use, as before
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(facts.dump())["conflicts"], facts.conflicts)

    def test_positions_revisions_and_requirements_are_watched_too(self):
        facts = case()
        facts.merge("positions", {"positions": [{"position": "1", "quantity": 4, "requirement_ref": "REQ-1"}]})
        facts.merge("positions", {"positions": [{"position": "1", "quantity": 40, "requirement_ref": "REQ-1"}]})
        facts.merge("revisions", {"revisions": [{"revision": "B", "status": "current"}]})
        facts.merge("revisions", {"revisions": [{"revision": "B", "status": "superseded"}]})
        facts.merge("requirements", {"revision": "B", "requirements": [{"requirement_ref": "REQ-1", "stroke_mm": 200}]})
        facts.merge("requirements", {"revision": "B", "requirements": [{"requirement_ref": "REQ-1", "stroke_mm": 250}]})
        facts.merge("requirements", {"revision": "C", "requirements": [{"requirement_ref": "REQ-1", "stroke_mm": 300}]})
        self.assertEqual([text.split(":")[0] for text in facts.conflicts],
                         ["position 1 quantity", "revision B status", "requirement REQ-1 in revision B stroke_mm"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

entries.name: mcp__atira__compare_runs
entries.description: Two runs side by side (A, then B, and how B differs): package, status, quality, time, cost, cost × time, calls and failures, phase times, calls and cost per model, the score's points per field that changed, and the answer's fields that changed. About 1–2k tokens.

a.description: The first run (A). A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

b.description: The second run (B), e.g. after a change. A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

entries.name: mcp__atira__run_llm_calls
entries.description: Every model call of a run, one line each: time on the run's clock, latency, queue wait (hosted models), model, status, tokens (cached), cost and id. The header has the time in calls, p50/p95 latency, the most calls at once, failures by status and the hosted models' queue waits. Filter by from/to, model and status (ok, error, all); page with after. About 35 tokens a call.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

from.description: The earliest start, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

to.description: The latest start, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

model.description: Only models whose provider/model contains this, e.g. qwen

after.description: Continue after a call id (c_123), e.g. the previous page's next

entries.name: mcp__atira__run_screenshot
entries.description: A browser's screen at a time in the run, cut from its recording, with the clicks just before it marked (red: the latest) and the log lines around it. browser "all" puts every browser in one 2×2 image; frames {from, to, every} makes a filmstrip of up to 9 frames in one image. While a run is still going there is no recording yet: it shows the latest live frame. About 1.5k tokens an image.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

at.description: When, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works. Not needed with frames.

browser.description: Which browser, 1–4 (default 1), or "all" for every browser at once

frames.description: A filmstrip instead of one frame: {from, to, every}, times on the run's clock (every: e.g. 10s)

marks.description: Mark the clicks recorded just before (default true)

Getting started

# From sign-in to your first scored run

How to sign in, set up and test your agent, and get it on the leaderboard. Limits and scoring are at the bottom.

Fastest start: point Claude Code or Codex at this site. Paste this, and it installs the CLI, connects itself, and helps you build, test and submit:

```
Read https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt, then set us up and help us build, test and submit an agent for this challenge.
```

Copy

[Sign in→](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) [The challenge→](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq)

## What you're building

Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

## Your first test run

Seven steps. The first five get your agent running against the websites. Step 6 tests it in the sandbox; step 7 puts it on the leaderboard.

1. 1


### Step 1: Sign in and form a team



[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.

2. 2


### Step 2: Install the CLI and sign in



The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ( [MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).





macOS and Linux







```
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
atira login
```

Copy









Windows, in PowerShell







```
irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex
atira login
```

Copy









Optional: connect the coding agent you use



Claude Code







```
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp
```

Copy





Codex







```
codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp
```

Copy

3. 3


### Step 3: Scout the websites yourself



Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored. Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)








| Website | URL | Username | Password |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tender portalVergabeportal | [atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run](https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run/) | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
| Supplier portalLieferantenportal | [atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run](https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run/) | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
| ERP | [atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run](https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run/) | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
| WebmailWerkpost | [atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run](https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run/) | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |

4. 4


### Step 4: Choose your starting point



Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.





macOS and Linux







```
mkdir my-agent
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C my-agent
```

Copy









Windows, in PowerShell







```
mkdir my-agent
curl.exe -fsSL -o starter-kit.tar.gz https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz
tar -xzf starter-kit.tar.gz -C my-agent
```

Copy

5. 5


### Step 5: Develop locally



You need uv for the starter kit ( [install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).





macOS and Linux







```
cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

Copy









Windows, in PowerShell







```
cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```

Copy







Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).

6. 6


### Step 6: Test in the sandbox



The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.







```
atira test-run .
```

Copy

7. 7


### Step 7: Submit



A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).







```
atira submit .
```

Copy


## Unlimited Inference

We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

- ### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next



#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.



LimitsNo usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.



Simulated pricing


| Input | $0.15 / M tokens |
| Cached input | $0.016 / M tokens |
| Cache writes | Free |
| Output | $0.47 / M tokens |





Precision[NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)



Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.







```
import os
from openai import OpenAI

qwen = OpenAI(
      base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
      api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
)
reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
      model="qwen",
      messages=[{\
          "role": "user",\
          "content": "Which button submits?",\
      }],
)
```

Copy

- ### Cloudflare Clef



A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev/). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.



LimitsNo usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.



Simulated pricing


| Input | $0.24 / M tokens |
| Output | Not priced |





Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.







```
curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
    "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
    "questions": {"next": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "What next?",
      "criteria": {
        "retry": "Retry the request",
        "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
```

Copy


In a run and on your machine

In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.

```
atira login   # once per computer
atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
export QWEN_API_KEY=local
export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
export CLEF_API_KEY=local
```

Copy

Cost and time count toward your rank, and a call to these models costs a fraction of a frontier call. Use them for the easy steps.

If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.

## Limits

What every scored run gets.

Scored run20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team.

Setup and networkSetup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy.

ModelsBring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

BrowsersAt most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs.

Sandbox4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo.

PackageUp to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup.

Fair playThe answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md).

TeamUp to 5 people.

## How you're scored

Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.

Quality

0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.

Eligibility

The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.

OrderEligible first→Quality ↓→Cost × time ↑

Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

## Public and private data

The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

## Using a coding agent?

Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.

Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.

Claude Code

```
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp
```

Copy

Codex

```

```

## Limits

What every scored run gets.

Scored run20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team.

Setup and networkSetup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy.

ModelsBring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

BrowsersAt most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs.

Sandbox4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo.

PackageUp to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup.

Fair playThe answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md).

TeamUp to 5 people.

## How you're scored

Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.

Quality

0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.

Eligibility

The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.

OrderEligible first→Quality ↓→Cost × time ↑

Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

## Public and private data

The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

If one fails mid-run, retry the call, as with any provider. If they were down for most of a run that then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count, and a scored run starts again once by itself.

## Limits

What every scored run gets.

Scored run20 minutes on the clock. Each submission runs once; one submission in flight per team.

Setup and networkSetup doesn't count toward your time: it has network access and up to 5 minutes to install what you need. The timed run reaches only the platform, the websites and the model proxy.

ModelsBring your own keys as team secrets, for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

BrowsersAt most 4 Chromium browsers at a time, provided by the sandbox; any number of tabs.

Sandbox4 vCPU, 8 GB memory and 30 GB disk on AMD Zen 5; 1280×800 screens. Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, Rust with cargo.

PackageUp to 20 MB compressed, with `agent.json` at the root. Its `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls (`["qwen", "clef"]` when absent); the run waits only for those to warm up, and `"models": []` starts it right after setup.

Fair playThe answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md).

TeamUp to 5 people.

## How you're scored

Every scored run gets a quality and an eligibility verdict; the platform measures its cost and time.

Quality

0 to 100. Every field of the bid is compared with the one correct answer: tender reference, positions, materials, quantities, unit prices, lead times, discount and total, each position's base price and surcharge per piece, packaging, allocated project bonus, and whether the total adds up.

Eligibility

The right tender reference; a wrong decision loses quality points but other correct fields keep their credit. A bid that is not eligible ranks after every eligible one.

OrderEligible first→Quality ↓→Cost × time ↑

Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality. At equal quality, the lower product of cost and time wins, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time as at least 1 s, so among free runs the faster one wins.

On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

## Public and private data

The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too. When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

## Using a coding agent?

Point it at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt); the home page, Getting started, each challenge, its leaderboard and each team's profile are also Markdown (add `.md` to the URL, `/index.md` for the home page), the API is described in [openapi.json](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json), and the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) shows every call with curl.

Or plug the CLI in as an MCP server: your agent lists your runs, queries their logs by time, sees a browser's screen at any moment, starts test runs and, once you confirm, submits. [Debug runs from your coding agent](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md) has the tools and other clients.

```
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp
```
